answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k², not k. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss as swarm size grows, making fabricated identities increasingly costly; asymmetric depreciation prevents rapid recovery of slashed stake. The glacier-like lockup and ferrous collateral rules are protocol terms, not a fable of costless anonymity: every linked signer risks its bond.
